narrative:
The model estimated a 53% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that risk estimate was high enough to cross the school’s denial threshold, your application was rejected. This is a forecast based on patterns in prior students’ records, not a statement that failure is certain.

The most influential factor was your plan to study part-time. Among accepted students, 92.8% were full-time and only 7.2% were part-time, and your part-time status pushed the prediction toward failure. The second factor was your first-year class standing: you were in decile 8, compared with an accepted-student average of 6. That factor pushed toward passing. Your third-year standing, decile 6 versus an accepted average of 5.79, was the third most important factor and also pushed slightly toward passing. Your gender and race were not used in the decision.

To move forward, ask admissions for feedback, meet with a prelaw advisor, and create a full-time study plan that reduces bar-exam risk. Consider LSAT preparation or a retake, since your 33 is below the accepted average of 37.18, and strengthen your academic record before reapplying.
